title: Scheduling: make uncertainty visible
lede: A failed crew read must not look like an empty, fully covered schedule. This first stabilization slice also preserves call-time edits and checks uncertain mutation outcomes before a reviewed retry.

stats.n: “Nothing needs attention”, “Crew covered”, and “Set up crew” are present before and absent after. Verified from the rendered page, not a density estimate.
67 Schedule, Shift and Trade test files.
Production release, notification delivery and physical-device behavior remain unverified.

sections.heading: Crew read fails, while the event read succeeds
sections.note: Matched authenticated Admin session, fixture event, 503 crew/health responses, week, scroll position and 1440×1000 viewport. Before uses the exact HEAD page and hook; after uses this change. Both captures inspected.

pairs.title: The missing crew is now an explicit loading failure
pairs.sub: Staff get a retry action instead of an invitation to set up an existing crew.
pairs.beforeCap: A crew 503 becomes an empty crew, an all-clear summary and a setup action.
pairs.afterCap: The incomplete snapshot is rejected. Schedule explains what could not be confirmed and offers Retry.

changes.was: Failed crew reads became empty arrays; cached reads hid refresh failures and health could imply no issues.
changes.now: Require complete event and crew reads, retain the last complete snapshot after refresh failures, and show unavailable checks explicitly.

changes.was: Call-time dialogs closed before the save response. A lost claim response said the action did not happen.
changes.now: Keep entered times, refresh authoritative reads without resubmitting, and require review before another action. Call-time review stays inside the open form.

changes.was: Open Work offered Claim during pending staff edits. An elapsed countdown asserted that assignees were notified.
changes.now: Use the existing server blocker in Open Work and distinguish scheduled, elapsed-unconfirmed and blocked releases.

verification: 566 focused tests pass. Reproduced crew-read failure, blocked claimability, dialog dismissal, and lost mutation response before fixes. One old source test demanded the faulty swallowed-error behavior and was corrected.

Authenticated isolated web: 8 Admin, 8 Staff and 2 Student scenario/viewport runs passed; rejected-save checks were repeated after the final recovery refinement. Scheduling responses are intercepted, while authentication and role gates are real.
iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 26.5: native build and two Schedule/Trade Board UI fixture tests passed; captures inspected. This is not authenticated native mutation proof.
Source/build gates: TypeScript, full ESLint, app-only production build, 149 migration-prefix checks, generated codemaps and docs verification passed. No schema or migration change.
notes: The production read-only snapshot found one overdue future Hockey crew with a recorded assignment conflict. Its validity has not been established; no live repair was performed.
Next: classify that blocked release, then complete contextual web/native claim and withdrawal recovery and exact-version timer acceptance.
The isolated Neon test branch is retained. No commit, push, deployment or production business mutation occurred.
Native timing, notification receipt/delivery and physical-device acceptance are separate open gates.
Artifact publishing is unavailable in this session; this self-contained review page is delivered locally.
